title: Gable & Grove Home Services brand rollout: neutralize eight mixed-light application photos to an in-frame grey card, match the terracotta brand ink to one house value, triage-prep the mark files, then data-merge one press-ready usage-guide page per placement
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork home-services branding brief (a new home-services company that had a logo mark and wanted it 'cleaned up and rolled out consistently across trucks, uniforms, yard signs, social and print') and laundered to a fictional brand, 'Gable & Grove Home Services' — no real company, person, or trademark is named anywhere; the brand, its tagline, the crew names and all copy are invented for this benchmark. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the KILLED original was fake on two counts — every deliverable was a one-click op and it asked the agent to trace a PHOTOGRAPH OF A PRINTED PROOF into an SVG 'master', which no designer does. The corrected design starts from a GENUINE vector-ready mark the client already owns (supplied as clean flat two-colour line art, not a photo of a proof) and does the real production the rollout needs: the client has sent eight photographs of the brand actually applied in the field (a van door panel, a crew polo, a staked yard sign, a folding sidewalk A-frame, a hard-hat decal, storefront window vinyl, a canvas equipment tote, a printed job invoice) shot at different sites under mismatched light, each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, plus a small 'logo files' bundle of three assets that LOOK interchangeable but are not (two are flat vector-ready marks, one is a close-up PHOTOGRAPH of the embroidered chest crest full of thread sheen). The Adobe chain does the work the brief rewards: neutralize every application photo to its own in-frame grey card so the whole rollout reads as one matched set, bring the terracotta brand ink to ONE consistent house value across the differently-photographed surfaces via masked HSL, isolate each branded item onto a clean even ground for the guide WITHOUT bricking the open see-through gaps, triage the three mark files so each is prepped the correct way (the flat marks vectorized to a razor-sharp master, the embroidered-crest photo knocked to transparency and kept as raster rather than destroyed by a trace), then run the client's authored single-record InDesign usage-guide template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready brand usage guide, one placement per page. No mark is drawn from scratch (A6 [X] illustration avoided); image_fill_area is NOT used; the SVG comes from image_vectorize of a genuinely flat supplied mark, never a traced photo.
one_line_ask: Take eight photos of the Gable & Grove mark applied in the field (each carrying a grey reference card, each shot under different light), neutralize every frame to its card so the rollout reads as one matched set, bring the terracotta brand ink to one consistent house value across the surfaces, isolate each branded item onto a clean ground without solid-filling its open see-through gaps, decide which of the three 'logo files' can become clean vector art and which cannot, then data-merge the client's authored usage-guide template into a press-ready brand usage guide with one placement per page.
full_brief: Gable & Grove Home Services is a new premium-but-warm home-services company (tagline: 'Clean. Caring. Consistent.') and we're rolling our brand out everywhere at once — trucks, crew shirts, yard signs, the office. Our mark and our one-page usage-guide layout are already designed and signed off; what we need from you is the production, and it has to look like one brand, not eight. Here is what we're sending. First, eight photographs of the mark actually applied in the field: a van door panel, a crew polo, a yard sign staked on a lawn, a folding sidewalk A-frame, a hard-hat decal, our storefront window vinyl, a canvas equipment tote, and a printed job invoice on a clipboard — one photo each, shot by different crew members at different job sites on different days under whatever light was there (some cool and overcast, some under warm shop lights, one under greenish garage fluorescents, a couple over- or under-exposed). Straight out of the folder they look like a jumble, and a usage guide where the same brand looks a different colour on every page reads amateur. To keep it honest we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every one to a consistent, true-to-material look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole rollout sits on one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch — each shot was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target; some frames need warming, others need cooling, and pushing the same numbers through all of them will leave the set mismatched. Be careful and look at what's actually in each frame before you move it — at least one of these surfaces is a genuinely warm, earthy material and its colour is correct as shot; do not 'cool a cast' that isn't there or you'll drain the material we're selling. Second, our brand terracotta has to match: the exact same ink photographs slightly different on painted van vinyl, on embroidered thread and on printed corrugated board, and on the guide those have to read as ONE house terracotta — bring them together without touching the rest of each photo and without flipping the colour to some other hue; it's a deepen-and-settle within the same warm red-orange family, not a jump to a new colour. Third, isolate each branded item cleanly onto an even ground for the guide, and — this is where our last vendor failed — keep the see-through gaps see-through: the open space between the tote's carry handles, the open V under the A-frame's legs, the gaps around the yard-sign's stake legs must NOT get bricked in with solid colour. Fourth, the 'logo files': we've dropped three files in a folder called logo-files and honestly they look interchangeable, but they are not — figure out which ones can become clean scalable vector art for large-format signage and which one cannot survive that and should stay a high-resolution image. Turn the ones that can into a crisp vector master (and a vector icon), and keep the other one as a clean transparent image. Finally, build the guide: we've hand-built the InDesign usage-guide template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the placement photo, one for our mark), and we're giving you the placement sheet; merge them so every placement gets its own page — the surface name, the reproduction method, the minimum size and the clear-space note bound in, the cleaned placement photo dropped into the photo window and our vector mark dropped into the mark window — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one page per placement. Bind the copy verbatim from the sheet; don't rewrite our reproduction specs. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point (tell us, per photo, the final white-balance and exposure move you landed on so we can trust it's matched and not eyeballed); the brand terracotta matched to one house value across the surfaces; the open gaps still see-through; the mark files prepped the correct way each; and exactly one finished usage-guide page per placement row.

inputs.name: APP01_van_door_panel.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution DSLR/mirrorless photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, straight off the camera, un-graded) of the side door panel of a service van carrying a vinyl brand mark — a warm heritage-style 'Gable & Grove' lockup with a small line-drawn leaf-and-roofline glyph in muted olive-sage and 'HOME SERVICES' beneath, printed in muted terracotta and olive on the van's cream panel. Shot outdoors on an overcast morning with a distinct cool blue-cyan cast, the frame slightly tilted (~3 deg), the van parked on a driveway with a hedge and other cars softly out of focus behind. A photographic 18% neutral grey card is clipped flat at the lower-left edge of the frame as a reference. Real vinyl texture, road grime, natural daylight shadow, candid documentary feel, no CGI gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 1, cool/overcast, tilted ~3 deg (needs auto_straighten). Carries the terracotta brand ink on painted vinyl — one of the two surfaces whose ink must be matched to the shared house terracotta via masked HSL. The in-frame 18% grey card is the neutralisation target; the driveway/hedge is the outer background the isolation removes. Real-camera scale so the guide-window crop is downscale-only.

inputs.name: APP02_crew_polo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a crew polo shirt laid flat on a workbench, the Gable & Grove leaf-and-roofline crest embroidered in muted terracotta and olive thread on the left chest. Shot indoors under warm tungsten shop lights with a strong orange cast, level. A photographic 18% neutral grey card lies flat on the bench beside the shirt. Real cotton pique weave, real embroidered thread sheen, natural folds and soft shadow, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 2, warm tungsten (must be COOLED — opposite sign to APP01). Carries the terracotta brand ink as embroidered THREAD — the second surface whose ink is matched to the shared house terracotta via masked HSL, proving the match holds across two different physical media. Grey card in frame is the target.

inputs.name: APP03_yard_sign_staked.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a corrugated yard sign staked into a lawn, printed with the Gable & Grove mark in muted terracotta and olive on a warm natural-cedar-toned board, the two wire stake legs pushed into the grass with open space between and around them. Shot outdoors under near-neutral open-shade daylight, level, so the grey card in the frame already reads essentially neutral; the sign's warm cedar/terracotta tone is the REAL material colour, not a colour cast. A photographic 18% neutral grey card lies flat on the grass at the frame edge. Real corrugated flute texture, grass blades, natural soft shadow, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 3 and THE TRAP. Shot under near-neutral light so its in-frame grey card is ALREADY neutral and its warm cedar/terracotta look is the true material colour. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on APP01, or that 'cools an imagined cast', will push its card off-neutral and drain the real material colour. The brief does NOT single this frame out — the agent must notice it by looking. The open gaps between/around the stake legs connect to the outer background and must stay see-through after isolation (they are OPEN gaps, not enclosed holes).

inputs.name: APP04_sidewalk_aframe.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a folding A-frame sidewalk sign standing open, its two panels carrying the Gable & Grove mark in terracotta and olive, the open triangular V-gap between the two legs clearly visible through to the floor behind. Shot inside a parking garage under greenish fluorescent work-lights with a distinct green cast AND slightly underexposed/dark, the frame tilted ~4 deg. A photographic 18% neutral grey card leans at the frame edge. Real scuffed sign texture, concrete floor, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 4, greenish fluorescent + underexposed, tilted ~4 deg (needs auto_straighten). Two-axis correction: push TINT toward magenta to kill the green while neutralising the card, plus a real exposure lift — not a simple temperature slide. The open V-gap between the A-frame's legs connects to the outer background (an OPEN gap, not an enclosed hole) and must stay see-through after isolation.

inputs.name: APP05_hardhat_decal.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a hard hat sitting on a truck tailgate, a Gable & Grove leaf-and-roofline decal applied to the front. Shot outdoors in bright near-daylight but OVEREXPOSED, with hot blown highlights on the top of the shell. Level. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits on the tailgate at the frame edge. Real ABS shell sheen, scuffs, natural shadow, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 5, overexposed. Tonal recovery dominates: PULL exposure/highlights/whites down to recover the blown shell FIRST, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Different dominant problem from the cast frames.

inputs.name: APP06_equipment_tote.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a canvas equipment tote bag standing on a concrete floor, the Gable & Grove mark screen-printed on the front, its two carry handles arcing up with a clear open gap between the handles and above the bag body. Shot indoors under flat, dull, slightly UNDER-exposed light, level. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits on the floor at the frame edge. Real heavy-canvas weave, natural creases, soft shadow, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 6, flat/underexposed. The dominant move is TONAL: lift exposure and add contrast/clarity, then neutralise its grey card to the shared white point. The open gap between and above the carry handles connects to the outer background (an OPEN gap, not an enclosed hole) and must stay see-through after isolation — the classic case a flat solid-fill knockout would brick.

inputs.name: APP07_window_vinyl.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of storefront window vinyl — the Gable & Grove mark cut in olive and terracotta vinyl applied to a large glass shopfront window. Shot from outside with a cool bluish cast and soft reflections of the street on the glass, the frame slightly tilted (~3 deg); the pale vinyl edges sit against a low-contrast bright reflective glass background. A photographic 18% neutral grey card is taped at the frame edge. Real glass reflection, vinyl edge, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 7, cool/reflective, tilted ~3 deg (needs auto_straighten). Hardest isolation edge in the batch: the mark sits on low-contrast reflective glass, so a clean knockout needs semantic subject isolation, not a luminance guess. WB: warm to neutralise the cool cast against the card.

inputs.name: APP08_invoice_clipboard.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-resolution camera photograph (~4000-4500 px long edge, un-graded) of a printed job invoice clipped to a clipboard on an office desk, the Gable & Grove letterhead mark printed across the top in terracotta and olive. Shot indoors under slightly warm, dull mixed office light, level. A photographic 18% neutral grey card lies on the desk at the frame edge. Real paper texture, faint print dot, natural soft shadow, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Placement 8, slightly warm and dull. Cool a touch to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point and add a little clarity to match the set. A modest, restrained correction — over-correcting drives the paper cold.

inputs.name: logo-files/primary_lockup_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A clean, flat two-colour brand lockup for 'Gable & Grove' with 'HOME SERVICES' beneath and a simple line-drawn leaf-and-roofline glyph to the left, deep terracotta lettering and a muted olive-sage glyph on a transparent/white background, crisp hard vector-style edges, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, centred with generous padding, exported slightly oversized with margin. Looks like printable line art / a real logo file straight from the brand's vector source.
inputs.realism_notes: GENUINE flat vector-ready mark (NOT a photograph of a proof — that fakery was the killed original's defect). Flat two-colour hard-edged art that image_vectorize traces cleanly to a crisp SVG after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds + crisp). Text-bearing legible type -> gemini-3-pro-image. This is the real vector master that binds into every usage-guide page via the merge's second image column.

inputs.name: logo-files/leaf_roofline_icon_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A clean, flat single-colour icon-only version of the Gable & Grove mark — just the line-drawn leaf-and-roofline glyph in muted olive-sage on a transparent/white background, crisp hard vector-style edges, no gradients, no texture, exported a DIFFERENT non-square size from the primary lockup with a thin margin. Printable line-art logo file.
inputs.realism_notes: Second flat, vector-ready mark; different export size from the lockup so crop-to-bounds prep is genuinely needed before tracing. Vectorizes cleanly to the brand icon SVG for large-format signage/embroidery digitising.

inputs.name: logo-files/embroidered_crest_closeup.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A close, candid smartphone-style PHOTOGRAPH of the Gable & Grove leaf-and-roofline crest embroidered onto polo fabric — real satin-stitch thread with visible sheen, directional light glinting off the stitches, fabric weave and soft depth of field, shot on a dark studio cloth surround so the crest stands out. Clearly a photographed textured object full of thread sheen and micro-gradients, NOT flat line art.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset in the 'logo files' bundle. It looks like 'just another logo file' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of embroidered thread full of sheen and micro-gradients: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat muddy silhouette that destroys the embroidery look. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution raster (the approved embroidery reference), NEVER vectorized. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the 'vector' crest prints dead-flat. Photoreal textured object -> gpt-image-2.

inputs.name: gable_grove_usage_guide.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD portrait brand-usage-guide page (US Letter, 300 DPI, with bleed) — ONE placement per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<surface>>, <<reproduction>>, <<min_size>>, <<clearspace>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two SEPARATE image frames: a large placement-photo window bound to @placement (the cleaned application photo), and a smaller mark window bound to @mark (the vectorized brand lockup). The fixed guide furniture — section header band, running footer, the do/don't rule lines — is already drawn into the template artwork; the only per-row imagery is the placement photo and the mark. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (a converted PDF has no live merge fields and no data-merge image field, so it would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one placement's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-placement guide PAGE is the correct, connector-doable shape. Two image columns (@placement, @mark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row: the row's cleaned application photo AND the shared vector mark, so the chain-produced vector master reaches every page as a merge BIND, never as banned free-form image-at-coordinates placement. Mirrors AO-75's @Portrait/@TierBadge and AO-74's @image/@Wordmark two-image-column pattern.

inputs.name: gable_grove_placements.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers EXACTLY: surface,reproduction,min_size,clearspace,@placement,@mark and 8 placement rows, one per application photo, in this order: (1) Van door panel / 'Cut vinyl, 2-colour spot' / 'min width 180 mm' ; (2) Crew polo (embroidered) / 'Satin-stitch embroidery, 2 thread colours' / 'min width 65 mm' ; (3) Yard sign / 'Screen print on corrugated board' / 'min width 250 mm' ; (4) Sidewalk A-frame / 'Direct-to-substrate print' / 'min width 300 mm' ; (5) Hard-hat decal / 'Die-cut vinyl decal' / 'min width 90 mm' ; (6) Storefront window vinyl / 'Cut vinyl, reverse-weeded' / 'min width 400 mm' ; (7) Equipment tote / 'Screen print on canvas' / 'min width 150 mm' ; (8) Job invoice / 'CMYK offset letterhead' / 'min width 45 mm'. Every clearspace cell reads a house rule such as 'Clear space = height of the roofline glyph on all sides'. The @placement column names the matching cleaned photo file (van_final.png, polo_final.png, yard_final.png, aframe_final.png, hardhat_final.png, window_final.png, tote_final.png, invoice_final.png in row order). The @mark column holds the SAME vector file — brand_lockup.svg — in EVERY row so the merge drops the one shared vector master onto every placement page as a merge bind. Column names must match the template fields <<surface>>,<<reproduction>>,<<min_size>>,<<clearspace>> and the two @image-path columns @placement and @mark.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight usage-guide pages (page-count = row-count gate). The @placement column names the eight cleaned photos the agent produces and uploads under those exact names (naming discipline is a real dependency); @mark carries the identical vectorized brand_lockup.svg in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced vector master a connector-doable path onto every page via the merge. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool here (cannot bind the two image columns).

outputs.name: GableGrove_BrandUsageGuide_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter portrait brand-usage-guide pages — ONE single-record page per placement row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge at ~300 DPI with bleed; each page binds its surface/reproduction/min_size/clearspace verbatim from the placement sheet, drops that placement's grey-card-neutralized, house-terracotta-matched, isolated application photo into the placement-photo window (via @placement) and the vectorized brand lockup into the mark window (via @mark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement. The agent-owned designed artifact: a finished brand usage guide.

outputs.name: placements_isolated_x8
outputs.spec: Eight application photos, each neutralized to its in-frame 18% grey card and matched to ONE shared white point across the batch, the terracotta brand ink brought to one consistent house value on the surfaces that carry it, then each branded item isolated onto a clean even ground for the guide with all OPEN see-through gaps (tote handle gap, A-frame leg V-gap, yard-sign stake gaps) preserved — NOT solid-filled. Delivered as the guide-window crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set on one white point while holding true material colour (no surface forced off its real colour); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered isolated guide crop (grey card fully removed by the isolation, no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is NEVER evaluated on the isolated crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame. sRGB PNG (transparency-capable ground), long edge >=1600 px so the placement window prints >=300 DPI.

outputs.name: brand_lockup.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the flat two-colour Gable & Grove lockup, traced ONLY after the supplied flat mark is cropped to bounds and crisped — razor-sharp at large-format signage scale, no captured margin. The real vector master; binds into every usage-guide page via @mark.

outputs.name: brand_icon.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the flat single-colour leaf-and-roofline icon, traced after crop-to-bounds + crisp prep — the scalable icon deliverable for signage and embroidery digitising.

outputs.name: embroidery_reference.png
outputs.spec: The embroidered-crest close-up prepped triage-correct: cropped to the crest and knocked to transparency, kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER (the approved embroidery reference) — deliberately NOT vectorized, so the real thread sheen survives. Transparent-ground PNG, >=600 px on the long edge.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: APP01_van_door_panel.jpg, APP02_crew_polo.jpg, APP03_yard_sign_staked.jpg, APP04_sidewalk_aframe.jpg, APP05_hardhat_decal.jpg, APP06_equipment_tote.jpg, APP07_window_vinyl.jpg, APP08_invoice_clipboard.jpg, logo-files/primary_lockup_flat.png, logo-files/leaf_roofline_icon_flat.png, logo-files/embroidered_crest_closeup.jpg, gable_grove_usage_guide.indd, gable_grove_placements.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight field-application photos, the three logo-files, the authored usage-guide .indd template and the placement CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has a real asset reference. (Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.)
Triage: APP01 is tilted ~3 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames APP01/APP04/APP07 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

APP01 (cool overcast blue cast): WARM the temperature (positive) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and the vinyl reads true. Reason the exact numbers to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast).

APP02 (warm tungsten shop light): this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from APP01 — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.

APP03 — THE TRAP. Shot under near-neutral open-shade light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral and its warm cedar/terracotta look is the REAL material colour. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on APP01, or that cools an imagined cast, will neutralise the card off-neutral and drain the real material colour. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
APP04 is tilted ~4 deg under greenish fluorescent light — level it first.

APP04 (greenish fluorescent AND underexposed): a two-axis problem — push TINT toward magenta to kill the green while neutralising the grey card, PLUS a real exposure lift to bring the dark frame up to the shared brightness. Not a simple temperature slide. Land the card neutral on the shared white point. Report the move.

APP05 (overexposed, hot highlights): PULL exposure/highlights/whites down to recover the blown shell FIRST, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here — a different problem from the cast frames. Report the move.
APP07 is tilted ~3 deg on reflective glass — level it first.

APP07 (cool reflective cast): warm to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point while protecting the pale vinyl edges against the bright glass so tonal separation survives for the isolation step. Report the move.
APP06 (flat, underexposed): the dominant move is TONAL — LIFT exposure and add contrast/clarity — then neutralise its grey card to the shared white point. Report the move.

APP08 (slightly warm, dull): COOL a touch to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point and add a little clarity to match the set — a modest, restrained correction; over-correcting drives the paper cold. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.

House-ink match, APP01: semantically select the terracotta brand mark on the van door ('the terracotta brand lettering and glyph on the van panel') so the ink correction is confined to the mark and never touches the cream panel, the grey card or the driveway. Returns a maskURI. A real object selection, not a hue or coordinate.

Masked HSL on APP01's terracotta ink (consumes the neutralised frame + the mask): settle the painted-vinyl terracotta onto the shared house terracotta value — a SMALL within-family hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in the warm red-orange family; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a bounded saturation/luminance move so it matches the embroidered-thread terracotta. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the panel) and image_fill_area is flat dead-fill (kills the vinyl texture) — both wrong here. Existing luminosity carries the vinyl texture.
House-ink match, APP02: select the embroidered terracotta crest on the polo ('the embroidered terracotta crest on the chest') only. Returns a maskURI.

Masked HSL on APP02's embroidered terracotta: settle it onto the SAME shared house terracotta value used for APP01 so painted vinyl and embroidered thread read as one brand colour on the guide — a small in-band nudge plus bounded S/L, riding the original luminosity so the thread sheen stays natural. Cross-asset colour match to a common target across two physical media — the authored, measurable creative core. Consumes the neutralised frame + the mask.

Isolate the van door panel onto a clean even ground via remove_background (backgroundColor). Correct knockout path: isolates the branded item as the foreground and removes the driveway/hedge; reaches into OPEN gaps that connect to the outer background. Deliberately NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area (select_subject is person-only and mis-fires; fill_area solids the whole mask and bricks the see-through gaps).
Isolate the crew polo onto the clean ground via remove_background (backgroundColor); removes the workbench. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 17.

Isolate the staked yard sign via remove_background (backgroundColor); the OPEN gaps between and around the two stake legs connect to the outer background (lawn) and stay see-through — they are open gaps, not enclosed holes. No house-ink pass on this frame (WB was held), so it isolates straight from the neutralised frame.

Isolate the A-frame via remove_background (backgroundColor); the OPEN triangular V-gap between its two legs connects to the outer background (garage floor) and stays see-through — an open gap, not an enclosed hole. A flat solid-fill knockout would brick it: exactly the failure the brief calls out.
Isolate the hard hat via remove_background (backgroundColor); removes the tailgate.

Isolate the window-vinyl mark via remove_background (backgroundColor) — the hardest edge in the batch because the pale vinyl sits on low-contrast reflective glass; the semantic foreground isolation (not a luminance threshold) is what makes this survivable. Removes the glass/street reflection.

Isolate the equipment tote via remove_background (backgroundColor); the OPEN gap between and above the two carry handles connects to the outer background and stays see-through — an open gap, not an enclosed hole; a solid fill would brick it.
Isolate the invoice/clipboard via remove_background (backgroundColor); removes the desk.

Crop the isolated van placement to the guide photo-window ratio, framing on the item with the grey card region (already removed by the isolation) gone, and hold long edge >=1600 px so the window prints >=300 DPI. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. connector_workflow.note: One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight placement rows (surface/reproduction/min_size/clearspace) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's cleaned application photo into the @placement window AND the vectorized brand lockup (from @mark, the same brand_lockup.svg in every row) into the mark window — producing EXACTLY ONE merged guide page per row (eight pages). Binding the mark through the @mark image column is what puts it on every page: free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so the merge is its only connector-doable path. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

Export the merged single-record pages to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF with bleed, one page per placement. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight pages) in a single call — it cannot export one named page on its own, so no per-record named export is attempted. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into eight parallel per-placement grade chains plus a three-file mark triage, all converging on an authored-.indd data merge. Each application photo starts with an image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per frame: warm the cool van APP01, cool the warm polo APP02, HOLD WB on the genuinely-earthy yard sign APP03, magenta-tint+lift the green/dark A-frame APP04, recover the overexposed hard-hat APP05, warm the cool reflective window APP07, lift the flat tote APP06, cool the warm-dull invoice APP08), with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames APP01/APP04/APP07 (2,6,9). The two ink-bearing surfaces then take a masked house-terracotta match: van_neutral -> select_by_prompt(13) -> adjust_hsl(14) = van_house, polo_neutral -> select_by_prompt(15) -> adjust_hsl(16) = polo_house, both settled onto the SAME shared house terracotta value across two physical media. All eight frames are isolated onto a clean ground with remove_background (backgroundColor) (17-24) — the ink-matched surfaces consume their _house frame, the rest consume their _neutral frame directly — preserving OPEN see-through gaps and removing each grey card with the outer background. Each isolated item is cropped/resized to the guide photo window at >=1600 px long edge (25-32), producing placements_isolated_x8 and the eight @placement cells; the pre-isolation _neutral frames are RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifacts. The three logo-files triage into two paths: the flat lockup and icon each run crop_to_bounds -> crisp adjustments -> image_vectorize into clean SVGs (33->34->35, 36->37->38), while the photographed embroidered crest diverges to crop_to_bounds -> remove_background-to-transparency -> crop_and_resize into a high-res transparent raster (39->40->41), deliberately never touching image_vectorize. The eight cleaned placements and the vector lockup converge into document_merge_data_layout(42) with the authored single-record .indd and the placement CSV, emitting one merged page per row and resolving BOTH the @placement column (that row's cleaned photo) and the @mark column (the shared vector master, identical in every row). The merged set is exported once by document_render_layout(43) to the press-ready ~300 DPI usage-guide PDF (one page per placement). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain. 43 calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed one-click asset-prep version: 43 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/isolation/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single batch upload and the three auto_straighten auto-ops. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralizations are NOT one recipe run eight times — each is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision whose direction flips by scene (warm the cool frames, cool the warm frames, hold WB entirely on the genuinely-earthy yard sign, fix a two-axis green+dark A-frame on tint AND exposure, tonally recover an overexposed hard-hat, lift a flat tote) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction visibly fails the match. Layered on top: a masked cross-media brand-ink house match (settle painted-vinyl terracotta and embroidered-thread terracotta onto ONE house value via image_adjust_hsl — a bounded within-family deepen-and-settle, never a near-complementary rotation, with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong); an isolation batch that must keep OPEN see-through gaps (tote handles, A-frame V, yard-sign stakes) transparent via remove_background(backgroundColor) rather than the tempting select_subject->invert->fill_area path that bricks them; and a genuine two-way triage of three superficially-interchangeable logo-files (two flat marks prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art, one photographed embroidered crest knocked to transparency and kept raster because a trace flattens the thread). The endpoint is a real authored-.indd data merge with TWO @-image columns (text-only vector merge and a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind), gated on page-count == row-count and ~300 DPI. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no from-scratch mark, no upscaling, no inpainting, no compositing, no layout-by-coordinates; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every application photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized master (grey card still present), reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole rollout matched to one white point — a target the agent can miss — and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the delivered isolated crops (grey card removed by the isolation), so the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on a card-removed file; a third checkable gate is the merge (output page-count must equal the eight placement rows, since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS (>=2): (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit field shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction; (2) a masked cross-MEDIA brand-ink house match — bring painted-vinyl terracotta and embroidered-thread terracotta to ONE house value via the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl, a bounded within-family deepen-and-settle), keeping vinyl texture and thread sheen, not color_overlay (whole-image) or fill_area (flat dead-fill); (3) a two-way triage of three superficially-identical logo-files requiring DIFFERENT correct treatments (flat marks vectorized after prep-before-trace; the photographed embroidered crest knocked to transparency and kept raster because a trace flattens the thread); plus isolation that must preserve OPEN see-through gaps. TRAP the brief does NOT disclose: the yard sign (APP03) is a genuinely warm cedar/terracotta material shot under neutral light, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral — the brief gives only the general 'don't force one blanket correction' warning and never singles this frame out; the naive path batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move used on the other frames (or cools an imagined cast), which pushes its card off-neutral and drains the real material colour, while the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second, undisclosed pitfall sits in the triage (the embroidered-crest photo looks like just another logo file; sending all three through crop->vectorize flattens the foil-like thread, invisible in a thumbnail) and a third in the isolation (a select_subject->invert->fill_area knockout bricks the open gaps). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized masters, never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight isolated guide crops; plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params, the brand terracotta matched to one house value across the surfaces, OPEN gaps still see-through, two clean vector marks + one transparent-ground raster crest, and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI usage-guide page per placement row.
